channel: block-access-lists/_threads/Hey everyone, I have been working on a
searchText: I believe it is just due to the order of checks in the spec, which results in a false depedency on the authority account. All gas checks are performed before the balance is assessed - in yellow paper also I believe this is true. This is the reason it's still in BAL because these were touched when assessing the gas. OOG / exceptional halt check on the instruction takes precedence to insufficient funds / balance check Yes, but reading the delegated account's state and it's code is not a part of gas checks, no? Only checking if it is warm/cold is required for gas checks It would create some efficiencies I think, though, if we could check balance earlier I see, let me check the exact test case you referenced my impl works something like ```diff diff --git a/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/vm/instructions/system.py b/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/vm/instructions/system.py index 14a8bd133..00f37d267 100644 --- a/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/vm/instructions/system.py +++ b/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/vm/instructions/system.py @@ -455,9 +455,6 @@ def call(evm: Evm) -> None: if code_address not in evm.accessed_addresses: evm.accessed_addresses.add(code_address) - code_hash = get_account(tx_state, code_address).code_hash - code = get_code(tx_state, code_hash) - # TODO: Consider consolidating charge_gas + charge_state_gas into # a single gas charge to avoid duplicate EVM trace entries. # Applies here and in create, create2, selfdestruct. See #2526. @@ -491,6 +488,9 @@ def call(evm: Evm) -> None: evm.gas_left += message_call_gas.sub_call evm.state_gas_left += call_state_gas_reservoir else: + code_hash = get_account(tx_state, code_address).code_hash + code = get_code(tx_state, code_hash) + generic_call( evm, message_call_gas.sub_call, ``` but for all CALL* opcodes, obviously Yes I see your point I think there is some reasoning here that we charged the gas for the access, therefore we have accessed it. But technically you don't need to do so if there isn't enough funds, you only need to assess whether there is enough for COLD / WARM and if it can succeed, only then do you need to actually load it. could be an easy optimization I'm not sure if this exact case was discussed, but I believe the reason is something like "we charged for access therefore we access it". I think there is room for making this optimization for sure... but we'd have to all agree on this. Yeah, of course, I just wanted to bring it up. It's a good point. I think it's worth discussing.
